pages.title: Plan an overland route and share it
pages.intro: Build a return route before taking a long expedition. This pack changes both terrain and movement; a single movement trick is not a substitute for supplies.

steps.label: 1. Make a starter walking stick
steps.text: Follow the crude-stick recipe: three sticks on a diagonal, with a rope immediately left of the centre stick (pattern __S / RS_ / S__). Its pack config grants AutoStep and a hunger modifier of -5; unlike better sticks, it has no WalkingSpeed entry. Equip it as a walking aid; the native guide describes passive bonuses while equipped.

steps.label: 2. Choose a forgiving route
steps.text: Scout a route back to shelter before trying cliffs. Terrain is affected by Watersheds, Rivers and Terra Prety. Mountain climbing is configured for Stone and Ore materials, with climb stamina cost 5 per second and jump stamina cost 20. Charged jumping has maxCharge 0.15 and sprint-jump disabled. Test movement on low ground; these pages do not prescribe unverified default keybinds.

steps.label: 3. Build a shared waypoint station
steps.text: Make a cartography table using its native recipe. Take the quill by right-clicking the ink-and-quill on the placed table. With the quill, right-click its map to write your changes; Ctrl + right-click reads the table changes into your map. Each table has its own shared waypoints; deletions are copied too.

steps.label: 4. Make repeat journeys easier
steps.text: Use the same path repeatedly to develop a trail. Only players create trails here; TrailDevolveDays is 60 and TrampledSoilDevolveDays is 4, so paths are not permanent. For group exploration, the advanced cartography table also shares explored areas; the ordinary table shares waypoints.

pages.title: Prepare, cross, and secure a vessel
pages.intro: Use the native Rough Seas guides for vessel-specific repairs and bailing. Quiet Rough Seas changes some behaviour, so these are not unmodified vanilla boats.

steps.label: 1. Check the water before launching
steps.text: Watch the wind, treetops, darkening sky and swell. Plan a short crossing with a sheltered landing, and turn back as storms approach. Rough Seas describes lightning and dangerous surf; a boat is not a safe place to wait out a storm.

steps.label: 2. Pack for the actual vessel
steps.text: Read Vessels and Their Repair, inspect the hull, and take its repair materials plus a bowl or bucket for bailing. Different vessels have different repair requirements; do not assume one repair material works for every hull.

steps.label: 3. Do not depend on river propulsion
steps.text: Quiet Rough Seas sets RiversPushBoats to false and both paddling/sculling stroke multipliers to 8. Its metadata also restricts boat hit damage to axes. That does not make a hull stormproof or replace repairs. Swimming/armour-load advice and patch-specific keys are deliberately omitted pending code-level verification.

steps.label: 4. Moor before stepping ashore
steps.text: With a rope, right-click the vessel and then a fence post ashore. Use the rope tool-mode control to adjust its length; a longer rope permits a wider swing. A sailboat can instead lower its anchor by right-clicking it with an empty hand, and raise it the same way. Storms can drag or break moorings: leave valuables ashore.

pages.title: Prepare a recovery kit before a fight
pages.intro: Combat Overhaul, Armory and Downed change the risk of travel. Prepare healing and a retreat before hunting or fighting; do not treat surviving defeat as free healing.

steps.label: 1. Make a small healing reserve
steps.text: Place two flax twine vertically in the crafting grid to make two clean bandages. Keep them accessible before leaving shelter. The clean bandage is a real healing item, not an ingredient-only preview.

steps.label: 2. Check the combat settings
steps.text: This pack enables melee swings stopping on terrain, while spear directional attacks are disabled. Spear aiming difficulty and thrown-distance settings are both 1. Vanilla armour grid recipes are disabled, so use the current item recipes rather than treating the vanilla armour guide as authoritative. Practise in open ground and use the current weapon controls shown by the game rather than a guessed attack key.

steps.label: 3. Retreat with a recovery plan
steps.text: Downed duration is 300 seconds here, self-revive is disabled and the map is hidden while downed. Passed-out recovery is also disabled. Agree where companions should regroup before splitting up. Do not promise automatic recovery: the exact rescue interaction is not established by this config and is not invented here.

steps.label: 4. Track and recover cautiously
steps.text: Blood Trail adds blood trails to animals wounded by a player. Follow tracks only when the return route and your remaining healing are adequate. Immersive Corpse Drop makes harvested corpse contents drop without a loot UI, so check the ground after harvesting rather than waiting for a container window.

pages.title: Agree a currency and make a small trade
pages.intro: Coins and Coinage are separate systems. Player-issued notes are not automatically metal coins or trader gears. Agree on the issuer and denomination before posting a price.

steps.label: 1. Found a note currency
steps.text: Craft and place a Coins mint using its native recipe, then right-click it. Choose a name, a 2–4 letter symbol and a colour. Your first personal currency is free. Mint a small quantity of 1-notes first; unlimited minting does not guarantee anyone will accept them. This pack permits at most three currencies per player.

steps.label: 2. Store money without hiding your payment
steps.text: Deposit notes by dragging them onto a wallet, or open the wallet and choose Deposit all notes. Withdraw before buying at a note-accepting shop: the Coins guide says shops take loose notes, not wallet balances. Losing the wallet loses its contents.

steps.label: 3. Make the exact change
steps.text: A shop asking for five 1-notes will not take a 10-note. Craft one 10-note into ten 1-notes, or one 100-note into ten 10-notes. Different currencies never mix. Use the Coinage guide separately for metal coin-making; no exchange rate between the two mods is established. Coinage requires hammer tool tier 3. Food still decays in Vinconomy shops here (stall perish rate 0.015).

steps.label: 4. Coordinate a group
steps.text: At a bound mint the founder can add players under Shared with. They can mint that currency, but cannot rename or transfer it. Use a notice board to advertise issuer, denomination and meeting place; its UI provides Compose notice. Ownership and posting permissions still apply. Tabletop Games is optional social play, not a prerequisite for trading. For Hand to Hand, the config requires the receiver to hold R; one-sided forced handoff is disabled.
